card.name: Word-initial t after a break
card.fires_on: A lone t or T (or hyphen-t) that begins a word, right after a hyphen, quote, space or prefix, so the word is split just before its first letters. Also fires on a few words like Senate and 'and' in title-like lists.

modes.label: Split-off t
modes.description: A single t or T begins a word that is split after a hyphen, quote or space.

modes.label: Capital T in names
modes.description: A capital T starts a brand or title word that is split into pieces.

modes.label: Legal-style list words
modes.description: Senate or and appears in titles of laws or committees.
modes.example: HIPAA Administrative Simplification Statute<< and>> Rules

card.plain: It fires when a word starts with a stray letter t that has been split off from the rest of the word.
